title: perf(canary): improve auto-detection thresholds & rollout guards for latency regressions
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: Our perf canary system detects regressions on latency and throughput but has produced a number of noisy alerts as traffic patterns change. This PR contains algorithmic and operational changes to reduce false positives and add strong rollout guards to prevent automatic rollouts when SLO-impacting regressions are detected.

Summary of changes: 1) Adaptive thresholding: replace static p99 delta thresholds with a traffic-aware, distributional approach. We now compute a time-weighted baseline distribution and trigger on statistically significant deviations (Welch's t + bootstrap for tail validation) instead of single-threshold comparisons. This reduces sensitivity to short-term variance during traffic spikes. 2) Multi-metric detection: introduce a combined signal that considers p50/p95/p99 latency shifts plus throughput and error-rate covariates. The detection rule requires at least two correlated signals to fire (configurable via canary policies). 3) Rollout guards: new blocking guard integrated into the rollout controller. If the canary detector reports a confirmed regression (p99 increase > adaptive bound AND throughput drop > 10% OR error rate increase > 0.5%), the rollout is paused and an automated rollback is triggered after a configurable grace period. 4) Observability: add per-canary dashboard panels (latency histograms, delta distributions, detection confidence) and a synthetic traffic harness for deterministic canary runs. 5) Tests and CI: unit tests for statistical routines, integration tests for rollout behavior (controller + detector), and an end-to-end canary simulation to validate guard behavior under controlled perturbations.

Why: We saw multiple noisy canary failures during regional traffic rebalancing that caused unnecessary rollbacks and pager fatigues (incident INT-2026-02-01). This implementation reduces noise while preserving sensitivity to real regressions, and makes guard actions auditable & reversible.

Implementation notes: - New module: perf/canary/detector.py implements the adaptive baseline and bootstrap tail checks. - Rollout controller change: infra/rollout/guards.yaml + controller hook to call detector API. - Metrics: added canary.detector.confidence and canary.detector.baseline_version counters for tracking. - Backwards compatibility: existing canary policies remain valid; behavior is opt-in via rolloutPolicy.reasoning: "adaptive_detection: true".

Testing: Extensive unit coverage added (perf/canary/tests/test_detector.py). Integration tests in perf-canary/e2e simulate traffic regressions and assert the controller pauses/reverts as expected. Local manual validation run against staging canary (canary-id: staging/rdw-frontend-2026-02) produced expected pauses and rollback decisions.

Migration / rollout: Default rollout policies remain unchanged. We will ship this behind a feature flag and enable for a subset of services for 2 weeks before broader rollout. Monitoring playbook updated in docs/perf-canary.md.

Risks & mitigations: - False negatives: bootstrap tail test aims to reduce missed regressions; we keep a conservative default confidence threshold and allow overrides per service. - Performance: detector runs are optimized and batched; added a rate limit to detector evaluation to keep controller CPU stable.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Dashboard panels - [x] Feature flag gating - [x] Linear tickets updated 

Related: ENG-2951 (adaptive canary algos), ENG-3010 (rollout controller safety), INT-2026-02-01 (incident follow-up).
